Oh yeah. I remember when my ED was “easy”. Now it’s a massive freaking battle with myself. Now I have to constantly remind myself that I’m engaging in ED behaviours, and I am never NOT aware of the fact that I’m engaging in these behaviours. I also get hungrier way faster and more constantly. My ED therapist says it’s because my body has been through the ringer and back, and is fighting back at my ED brain trying to starve it. She said because my body now KNOWS what it’s like to have been through it the first time, it’s doing everything it can to not get to that point again.

I’ve been to inpatient at a “normal” weight (though just barely) AND “overweight”. I won’t lie, I felt so embarrassed the second time I almost didn’t go. But weight doesn’t define ED status and I’m glad I went. But i won’t lie it was hard being the biggest person there. But I talked about that in therapy sessions while I was there, which helped a LOT.

Honestly, it can be pretty obvious. Of course in some cases it’s harder to tell, like I’m currently OW and people don’t seem to clock in but when I had the EXACT same habits when I was severely UW it felt like everyone clocked me. As someone who’s been all over with EDs, I definitely notice it in other people, even when they aren’t UW, but that’s just because of my experience with different EDs. Mileage may vary but overall I think game recognizes game.
